user.text: Migrate every route and file from the Pages Router to the Next.js App Router. When finished, remove the pages dir entirely. Ensure the proper App Router APIs are used. If a Pages Router API was used that no longer exists in App Router, replace it with the newer version or the new pattern. Make sure to add types.

1  	---
2  	title: route.js
3  	description: API reference for the route.js special file.
4  	---
5  	
6  	Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.
7  	
8  	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
9  	export async function GET() {
10 	  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })
11 	}
12 	```
13 	
14 	```js filename="route.js" switcher
15 	export async function GET() {
16 	  return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })
17 	}
18 	```
19 	
20 	## Reference
21 	
22 	### HTTP Methods
23 	
24 	A **route** file allows you to create custom request handlers for a given route. The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`.
25 	
26 	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
27 	export async function GET(request: Request) {}
28 	
29 	export async function HEAD(request: Request) {}
30 	
31 	export async function POST(request: Request) {}
32 	
33 	export async function PUT(request: Request) {}
34 	
35 	export async function DELETE(request: Request) {}
36 	
37 	export async function PATCH(request: Request) {}
38 	
39 	// If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
40 	export async function OPTIONS(request: Request) {}
41 	```
42 	
43 	```js filename="route.js" switcher
44 	export async function GET(request) {}
45 	
46 	export async function HEAD(request) {}
47 	
48 	export async function POST(request) {}
49 	
50 	export async function PUT(request) {}
51 	
52 	export async function DELETE(request) {}
53 	
54 	export async function PATCH(request) {}
55 	
56 	// If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
57 	export async function OPTIONS(request) {}
58 	```
59 	
60 	### Parameters
61 	
62 	#### `request` (optional)
63 	
64 	The `request` object is a [NextRequest](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) object, which is an extension of the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) API. `NextRequest` gives you further control over the incoming request, including easily accessing `cookies` and an extended, parsed, URL object `nextUrl`.
65 	
66 	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
67 	import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
68 	
69 	export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
70 	  const url = request.nextUrl
71 	}
72 	```
73 	
74 	```js filename="route.js" switcher
75 	export async function GET(request) {
76 	  const url = request.nextUrl
77 	}
78 	```
79 	
80 	#### `context` (optional)
81 	
82 	- **`params`**: a promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) for the current route.
83 	
84 	```ts filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.ts" switcher
85 	export async function GET(
86 	  request: Request,
87 	  { params }: { params: Promise<{ team: string }> }
88 	) {
89 	  const { team } = await params
90 	}
91 	```
92 	
93 	```js filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.js" switcher
94 	export async function GET(request, { params }) {
95 	  const { team } = await params
96 	}
97 	```
98 	
99 	| Example                          | URL            | `params`                           |
100	| -------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
101	| `app/dashboard/[team]/route.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |
102	| `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/route.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |
103	| `app/blog/[...slug]/route.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`    |
104	
105	### Route Context Helper
106	
107	You can type the Route Handler context using `RouteContext` to get strongly typed `params` from a route literal. `RouteContext` is a globally available helper.
108	
109	```ts filename="app/users/[id]/route.ts"
110	import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
111	
112	export async function GET(_req: NextRequest, ctx: RouteContext<'/users/[id]'>) {
113	  const { id } = await ctx.params
114	  return Response.json({ id })
115	}
116	```
117	
118	> **Good to know**
119	>
120	> - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`.
121	> - After type generation, the `RouteContext` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported.
122	
123	## Examples
124	
125	### Cookies
126	
127	You can read or set cookies with [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) from `next/headers`.
128	
129	```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
130	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
131	
132	export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
133	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
134	
135	  const a = cookieStore.get('a')
136	  const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1')
137	  const c = cookieStore.delete('c')
138	}
139	```
140	
141	```js filename="route.js" switcher
142	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
143	
144	export async function GET(request) {
145	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
146	
147	  const a = cookieStore.get('a')
148	  const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1')
149	  const c = cookieStore.delete('c')
150	}
151	```
152	
153	Alternatively, you can return a new `Response` using the [`Set-Cookie`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie) header.
154	
155	```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher
156	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
157	
158	export async function GET(request: Request) {
159	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
160	  const token = cookieStore.get('token')
161	
162	  return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', {
163	    status: 200,
164	    headers: { 'Set-Cookie': `token=[redacted] },
165	  })
166	}
167	```
168	
169	```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher
170	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
171	
172	export async function GET(request) {
173	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
174	  const token = cookieStore.get('token')
175

<content>
1  	---
2  	title: generateStaticParams
3  	description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
4  	---
5  	
6  	The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
7  	
8  	`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
9  	
10 	- [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
11 	- [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
12 	- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
13 	
14 	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
15 	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
16 	export async function generateStaticParams() {
17 	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
18 	
19 	  return posts.map((post) => ({
20 	    slug: post.slug,
21 	  }))
22 	}
23 	
24 	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
25 	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
26 	export default async function Page({
27 	  params,
28 	}: {
29 	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
30 	}) {
31 	  const { slug } = await params
32 	  // ...
33 	}
34 	```
35 	
36 	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
37 	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
38 	export async function generateStaticParams() {
39 	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
40 	
41 	  return posts.map((post) => ({
42 	    slug: post.slug,
43 	  }))
44 	}
45 	
46 	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
47 	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
48 	export default async function Page({ params }) {
49 	  const { slug } = await params
50 	  // ...
51 	}
52 	```
53 	
54 	> **Good to know**:
55 	>
56 	> - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
57 	> - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
58 	> - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
59 	> - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
60 	> - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
61 	> - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
62 	
63 	## Parameters
64 	
65 	`options.params` (optional)
66 	
67 	If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
68 	
69 	The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
70 	
71 	## Returns
72 	
73 	`generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
74 	
75 	- Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
76 	- The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
77 	
78 	| Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
79 	| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
80 	| `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
81 	| `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
82 	| `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |
83 	
84 	## Single Dynamic Segment
85 	
86 	```tsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
87 	export function generateStaticParams() {
88 	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
89 	}
90 	
91 	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
92 	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
93 	// - /product/1
94 	// - /product/2
95 	// - /product/3
96 	export default async function Page({
97 	  params,
98 	}: {
99 	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
100	}) {
101	  const { id } = await params
102	  // ...
103	}
104	```
105

107	export function generateStaticParams() {
108	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
109	}

43 	
44 	Dynamic metadata depends on **dynamic information**, such as the current route parameters, external data, or `metadata` in parent segments, can be set by exporting a `generateMetadata` function that returns a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields).
